rationale: Use colour and zero-based coordinates modulo 3. Zeros on row residue 0 and column residues 1 or 2 become 8; on row residue 2, column residue 1 becomes 2 and residue 2 becomes 5. Demonstration 2 shows all three replacements; nonzero colours stay unchanged.

Use own colour and the row's nonzero colour set. With set {2}, zeros become 2; with {2,3}, threes become 4; with {1,2,3}, zeros become 6 and threes become 8. Demonstration 4 exhibits all three cases; other row sets preserve colours.

Use own colour and the row's nonzero colour set. Zeros become 7 for {2} or {1,3}, and 4 for {1,2}; threes become 0 for {1,2,3}. Demonstration 1 shows {2} filling and three removal, while demonstration 2 shows both other zero replacements.

Use own colour and zero-based coordinate parity. On even rows, zeros in odd columns become 4, twos in odd columns become 1, and threes in even columns become 0. On odd rows, twos in even columns become 4. Demonstrations 1 and 3 exhibit these changes.

Use own colour and zero-based coordinate parity. Even-row odd-column zeros become 2; odd-row even-column zeros become 9 and twos become 6; even-row even-column threes become 1. Demonstrations 1, 2 and 5 show these replacements, with other parity-colour combinations preserved.

Use own colour and nearest nonzero colours in the four directions. Demonstration 4 changes the zero at (0,2) to 6, demonstration 6 changes (4,2) to 1, and demonstration 8 changes (3,6) to 6, using zero-based coordinates. Directional context distinguishes these sparse changes from unchanged zeros.

Use own colour and both row and column nonzero sets. Twos become 3 when the row and column both contain {1,2,3}; ones become 6 when the row contains {1,2,3} and the column {1,3}; zeros become 6 when the row contains {1,3} and the column {3}. Demonstrations 4, 8 and 6 show these cases.

Use own colour and nearest nonzero colours up, down, left and right. Demonstration 2 changes (1,1) from 0 to 3; demonstration 3 changes (1,0) and (2,0) to 8 and (5,1) from 3 to 6; demonstration 6 changes (2,4) to 6. These depend on directional context.

Use own colour and zero-based coordinates modulo 3. Zeros with row residue 1 and column residue 1 become 3. On row residue 2, zeros become 7, 9 or 1 for column residues 0, 1 or 2 respectively. Demonstration 1 shows the full replacement pattern; nonzero colours remain unchanged.

Use own colour and zero-based coordinate parity. All twos on even rows become 0; ones at even-row even-column positions become 9; zeros at odd-row odd-column positions become 1. Demonstrations 1 and 2 show these changes, while other combinations preserve their colours.
